name: When should I consider replacing my home's weatherstripping?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing my home's weatherstripping?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing weatherstripping when it shows signs of wear and tear, such as cracking, shrinking, tearing, or becoming brittle. A simple test is to hold a lit candle or incense stick near closed doors and windows on a windy day; if the flame flickers or smoke moves, you likely have air leaks. Replacing old weatherstripping can significantly improve insulation, reduce drafts, and help maintain consistent indoor temperatures, especially in older homes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace weatherstripping when it's cracked, brittle, or no longer seals effectively, which you can test for with a simple draft detection method.
